newsitem.title: USA: Lam Research sees worst problems behind it.
newsitem.headline: Lam Research sees worst problems behind it.

text.p: Lam Research Corp, a maker of seminconductor wafer processing equipment, Tuesday said it believes its own operational and market problems in fiscal 1997, ended June 30, have been put to rest.
"I am confident...the worst is behind us," Chief Executive Officer Roger Emerick said in a statement.

Earlier, Lam reported a fiscal fourth quarter loss of $0.06 a share, but that included a $0.15 per share after-tax charge. Excluding the charge, the company would have earned $0.09 a share, which is $0.01 per share ahead of analysts' consensus estimate of $0.08 a share, according to First Call.
Lam reported earnings of $1.27 per share in fiscal 1996's fourth quarter and a loss of $1.46 per share in third quarter of fiscal 1997.

New orders in the fourth quarter exceeded shipments and increased nearly eight percent to $292.2 million from new orders of $271.7 million in the prior quarter. New orders for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 1996 totaled $291.0 million.
Emerick said Lam continues to focus on increasing manufacturing efficiency placing an emphasis on inventory management, product standardization and cost reductions.
